sites.ownership: The application controller owns shared multi-window lifecycle state.
sites.justification: App actions and lifecycle signals route to the last-focused editor window and maintain a window registry without global statics.

sites.ownership: GTK tests reuse the shared application-state container.
sites.justification: The test harness drives the same window routing and activation paths as runtime code, including last-focused resolution.

sites.ownership: The application object owns this AppState handoff for app actions, activation, and startup restore callbacks.
sites.justification: The state is GTK-main-thread confined and each handler borrows it only for the short action/orchestration step needed to avoid duplicating application lifecycle state.

sites.ownership: Window registration mutates shared application state.
sites.justification: Destroy and focus notifications must add/remove windows and update last-focused tracking to keep action routing correct.

sites.ownership: Startup display service installation mutates shared application state.
sites.justification: The global chrome provider must be installed once a display exists and then stored in AppState so all later windows receive the same palette controller.

sites.ownership: AppChromeController tracks per-window observer callbacks via Weak references.
sites.justification: Observers fire on chrome refresh (palette/dark/HC change). Weak storage with compaction-on-add-and-refresh prevents stale callbacks after window close from leaking signal subscriptions or aborting on dropped state.

sites.ownership: AppChromeController owns the global libadwaita color provider and palette signal subscriptions for the entire application.
sites.justification: A single GtkCssProvider attached to gdk::Display::default() at startup overrides libadwaita CSS custom properties on :root. Subscriptions cover StyleManager dark + high-contrast and AppSettings editor-palette changes; recoloring is a no-op for high-contrast and Adwaita schemes.

sites.ownership: The close coordinator owns the active sequential close queue.
sites.justification: Unsaved tab-close, window-close, and quit flows need mutable queue progress without leaking state into the window shell.

sites.ownership: The encoding chooser owns its one-shot response callback for the dialog lifetime.
sites.justification: Accept, cancel, and close signals must share one callback slot so the encoding response is delivered at most once while avoiding widget-owned callback cycles.

sites.ownership: The encoding chooser owns its close/response guard.
sites.justification: The closed handler intentionally owns the dialog state, while accept and cancel paths set this guard before closing so close cannot call the one-shot callback again.

sites.ownership: The document portal resolver owns the process-local document ID to host-path cache and in-flight callback queue.
sites.justification: Display-path rendering must not block the UI on portal D-Bus calls, so async GetHostPaths results are coalesced and cached while portal access paths remain authoritative for I/O.

sites.ownership: The window's document tools controller owns remembered print dialog choices.
sites.justification: Print settings must survive between print runs in the same window so the user's paper and printer choices are not reset on every print.

sites.ownership: The window's document tools controller owns remembered print dialog choices.
sites.justification: Page setup must survive between print runs in the same window so the user's paper and orientation choices are not reset on every print.

sites.ownership: The print preview engine owns the in-flight preview operation state.
sites.justification: GTK delivers preview pagination and page-size callbacks asynchronously on the main loop, so the engine must share mutable state between signal closures and the dialog.

sites.justification: Dialog callbacks restart rendering, navigate pages, and clean up the active preview engine while GTK signals run on the main loop.

sites.ownership: The document tools controller owns the mutable print runner injection point.
sites.justification: Print action tests replace only this scoped runner while runtime action state remains owned by the window-local controller.

sites.ownership: The document tools controller owns the mutable print preview runner injection point.
sites.justification: Preview action tests replace only this scoped runner while runtime action state remains owned by the window-local controller.

sites.ownership: Each document monitor owns the removable polling source.
sites.justification: File-monitor events can be unreliable on portal-backed paths, so the binding keeps one cancellable polling source that is removed with the GIO monitor.

sites.ownership: Each document monitor owns one async file-stamp state machine.
sites.justification: GIO metadata queries complete asynchronously, so monitor events, polling fallback, cancellation, and stale-result guards must coalesce through one mutable state cell without blocking the GTK main loop.

sites.ownership: The find bar owns document/project search scope state and callback dispatch.
sites.justification: Search and replace callbacks share this main-thread state so document search, project dispatch, and scope toggles stay synchronized.

sites.ownership: The find bar owns document/project search scope state and the project-search dispatch hook.
sites.justification: Search UI callbacks need one shared main-thread state cell so Ctrl+F, Ctrl+H, Ctrl+Shift+F, scope toggles, and replace visibility cannot diverge.

sites.ownership: The search controller owns one mutable binding to the active tab and active search context.
sites.justification: Workspace-level search preserves query state while rebinding highlights, match counts, and replace state to the selected tab.

sites.ownership: The find bar owns document/project search scope state and the project-search dispatch hook.

sites.ownership: The status bar test harness owns the format-label update counter.
sites.justification: GTK regression tests need a main-thread-confined counter to verify redundant status label updates are skipped without depending on MenuButton child internals.

sites.ownership: Each editor tab owns one shared mutable state cell split into document runtime, IO, external-file, autosave, compare, and UI owner structs.
sites.justification: The tab facade coordinates cross-owner transitions such as writability, autosave pausing, banners, compare reference loading, and scratch-then-apply IO without introducing multiple independent RefCell borrows.

sites.ownership: Each editor tab owns its current workspace file-drop callback.
sites.justification: Tabs can move between windows, so file-drop routing must be replaceable without rebuilding the editor widget.

sites.ownership: Each editor tab owns its current workspace visual-state callback.
sites.justification: Cursor, dirty, and title updates must rebind to the destination workspace when a tab is transferred to another window.

sites.ownership: Each editor tab owns its current Markdown preview-state callback.
sites.justification: Preview enter, exit, and render events must rebind search state to the workspace that currently owns the tab after window transfer.

sites.ownership: Each editor tab owns its current external-state callback.
sites.justification: External file-change banners must update the workspace that currently owns the tab after window transfer.

sites.ownership: Each editor tab owns its current external-action callback.
sites.justification: Reload, save, and compare banner actions must route to the workspace that currently owns the tab.

sites.ownership: The minimap palette resolver owns a process-local cache keyed by libadwaita dark and high-contrast style state.
sites.justification: The cache is GTK-main-thread confined and stores deterministic colors probed from resource CSS so minimap rendering avoids repeating display-wide style-provider probes on every refresh.

sites.ownership: The minimap palette test harness owns the cache-miss counter.
sites.justification: GTK regression tests need a main-thread-confined counter to prove repeated minimap palette requests reuse the cached probe result without exposing runtime diagnostics.

sites.ownership: The compare controller owns the tab-local rendered presentation rows and custom line-number gutter model.
sites.justification: Read-only compare panes render from ephemeral presentation buffers, so custom gutters, hatch layers, and tests need one shared source of display-row to original-line mapping.

sites.ownership: The compare controller owns the tab-local collapsed display model shared by split rendering and hunk navigation.
sites.justification: Collapsed manual Compare needs one display-row map so split buffers, unified buffers, reveal state, and navigation resolve logical diff rows to the same visible rows.

sites.ownership: The compare controller owns the tab-local logical diff row model.
sites.justification: Presentation rendering, hunk navigation, status, and test accessors must share one ephemeral row model so manual Compare and Git compare cannot drift into parallel diff states.

sites.ownership: Each compare controller owns presentation and view-mode state shared with its pane, gutter, and breakpoint callbacks.
sites.justification: Compare panes rebuild asynchronously from user actions and settings changes, so small shared cells keep UI callbacks synchronized without global state.

sites.ownership: Each compare controller owns the tab-local user minimap visibility state shared with narrow-width breakpoint callbacks.
sites.justification: Compare panes need to suppress minimaps on narrow allocations while still honoring the user's global minimap preference when space returns.

sites.ownership: Each compare controller owns the tab-local narrow-width minimap suppression state shared with settings updates.
sites.justification: The compare minimap breakpoint must coordinate with later preference changes without global state or stale closure-local visibility.

sites.ownership: The compare controller layout helper returns the tab-local adaptive view-mode cell owned by the CompareController.
sites.justification: The helper is a construction boundary for the existing view-mode cell so controller initialization stays under the line cap without duplicating adaptive breakpoint state.

sites.ownership: The compare controller construction helpers use a local alias for the two per-controller minimap visibility cells.
sites.justification: The alias keeps constructor signatures compact while the cells remain owned by the CompareController and shared only with its breakpoint callbacks.

sites.ownership: The compare diff unit tests own one thread-local line-diff call counter.
sites.justification: The Finding 5.1 regression test must prove each non-large compare path uses one full line diff while avoiding cross-test interference under parallel cargo test execution.

sites.ownership: Compare gutter state owns a shared handle to the tab-local presentation line-number model.
sites.justification: Refreshing both gutters after compare recompute, zoom, and style changes needs the latest row map without copying per-pane line-number state.

sites.ownership: Compare gutter state owns a shared handle to the tab-local logical row model.
sites.justification: Custom gutter marker cells need the current row kind so equal rows reserve a blank marker column while reference/current changes render visual -/+ markers after recompute.

sites.ownership: Compare gutter setup borrows the controller-owned presentation line-number model.
sites.justification: Both gutter renderers need read-only access to the same presentation row map so placeholder rows stay blank without copying per-pane line-number state.

sites.ownership: Compare gutter setup borrows the controller-owned logical row model.
sites.justification: GtkSourceView queries gutter marker text per visible line, so the renderer callback must read the latest row kind after every recompute and keep visual +/- markers aligned with the active row model.

sites.ownership: The compare gutter renderer borrows controller-owned presentation state for visible-line mapping.
sites.justification: GTK gutter callbacks are invoked by SourceView during drawing and need shared immutable access to the latest diff presentation without copying it into each renderer.

sites.ownership: Compare hatch GTK test accessors own a shared handle to the tab-local presentation model.
sites.justification: Regression tests inspect visible hatch regions against the latest placeholder row map without copying per-pane presentation state; this field is test-only.

sites.ownership: Each compare hatch layer owns the cached high-contrast state shared with its draw callback.
sites.justification: Style changes update the cached value once, while the DrawingArea callback can render the high-contrast solid fallback without querying libadwaita on every frame.

sites.ownership: Each compare hatch layer owns an idempotent detach guard.
sites.justification: Compare exit and Drop can both reach overlay cleanup, so the Cell prevents duplicate widget unparenting without introducing a wider controller-level mutable borrow.

sites.ownership: The compare hatch overlay borrows the tab-local presentation model owned by the compare controller.
sites.justification: Visible filler-row drawing must follow the latest presentation rows without copying diff state or querying unrelated editor buffers from the draw callback.

sites.ownership: The compare hatch draw callback borrows the shared high-contrast flag.
sites.justification: The callback must see style refreshes without per-frame StyleManager queries, and the Cell keeps the cached render mode local to the hatch layer.

sites.ownership: Presentation pane interactions borrow the controller-owned presentation metadata.
sites.justification: Selection copy must replace generated placeholder marker rows with blank text while preserving clipboard line layout.

sites.ownership: The compare layout owns the adaptive breakpoint mode cell shared with breakpoint callbacks.
sites.justification: Breakpoint apply/unapply signals need to observe the current explicit mode so adaptive resizing does not override user-selected split or unified layout.

sites.ownership: Each compare minimap state owns the desired user-visible state shared with map/unmap callbacks.
sites.justification: The holder can become mapped or unmapped independently of preference changes, so callbacks need the latest intended visibility before attaching a GtkSourceMap view.

sites.ownership: Each compare minimap state owns an idempotent sync guard for attach/detach transitions.
sites.justification: GtkSourceMap view attachment can perturb GTK adjustment state; the guard keeps map/unmap callbacks from recursively re-entering the lifecycle sync.

sites.ownership: Each compare minimap state owns the latest requested minimap font description.
sites.justification: The map can be detached while zoom or font settings change, so reattachment must preserve the intended font state without querying stale widget state.

sites.ownership: The compare minimap width breakpoint owns a cloned handle to the tab-local user minimap visibility cell.
sites.justification: Breakpoint apply/unapply callbacks need the current user minimap preference so narrow-width suppression restores the correct state when the pane widens.

sites.ownership: The compare minimap width breakpoint owns a cloned handle to the tab-local narrow-width suppression cell.
sites.justification: Preference updates and breakpoint callbacks must share one per-controller suppression flag so hidden minimaps remain intentional only while the pane is narrow.

sites.ownership: Compare scroll synchronization owns a shared handle to the tab-local logical row model.
sites.justification: Programmatic first-hunk and hunk-navigation scrolls verify the target presentation row against the current row count without copying diff state into the scroll helper.

sites.ownership: Each large-file search owns one accumulator shared only by its sequential async window callbacks.
sites.justification: Carry and capped match offsets are updated within a scoped main-context borrow that ends before completion callbacks or recursive read dispatch, avoiding per-window vector copies and reentrant borrows.
